citations.claim: the URI is expected to work when scanned, usually a redirect
citations.evidence: DL §2 (Conformance, normative): "Applications SHALL NOT assume that a URL that follows the syntax defined in this standard will point to a resolver"; change log: "GS1 Digital Link URIs do not have to, and SHALL NOT be assumed to, point to a resolver". citations.claim: identity, net quantity, name and place of business
citations.evidence: 15 USC 1453(a)(1): "The commodity shall bear a label specifying the identity of the commodity and the name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor"; (a)(2): net quantity "separately and accurately stated in a uniform location upon the principal display panel ... using the most appropriate units of both the customary inch/pound system ... and ... the SI metric system"; 16 CFR 500.1: Part 500 "establish[es] requirements for labeling of consumer commodities ... with respect to identity ..., the name and place of business ..., the net quantity of contents".
21 CFR 101.9 and 21 CFR 101.4(a)(1): ingredients "shall be listed by common or usual name in descending order of predominance by weight".
No allergen-declaration requirement in Part 101 (sources 101.2-101.100 contain no "allergen"); it is FDCA 403(w), 21 USC 343(w) (enacted by FALCPA): "Major food allergen labeling requirements".

citations.claim: domain must be a real registered domain you control that resolves
citations.evidence: DL §2 (Conformance, normative): "Applications SHALL NOT assume that a URL that follows the syntax defined in this standard will point to a resolver"; change log: "GS1 Digital Link URIs do not have to, and SHALL NOT be assumed to, point to a resolver". GenSpecs 2.1.13.1 says only (descriptively) that DL "explicitly encodes a resolvable Web URI" and that example.com is "a place holder for any domain name". DL §3 says the hostname "is typically a registered Internet domain name" — descriptive, not a requirement.
